Expectation1: Provide guidance and wisdom based on life experience
Situation1: A grandchild directly asks their grandparent for help and advice with a serious concern in their life.
Expectation2: Fix bugs and troubleshoot issues reported by users or QA
Situation2: Several users report intermittent errors that disrupt normal usage
Story: I was sitting at the kitchen table, laptop open, fingers poised over the keyboard, when my phone buzzed with another error report. The app was acting up again—users were losing data, and the QA team was pinging me every few minutes. My mind raced through possible causes, but before I could dive into the logs, my granddaughter shuffled in, her face clouded with worry. She hesitated, then asked, “Grandpa, can I talk to you about something important?” I could see she needed me—really needed me—not just to listen, but to offer the kind of advice only a grandparent could give. At the same time, my inbox kept filling with urgent messages, each one a reminder of the responsibility I had to my team and our users. I felt torn, the weight of both worlds pressing in. My granddaughter’s eyes searched mine for reassurance, while my mind screamed about deadlines and broken code. I wanted to be fully present for her, to offer the wisdom she sought, but the demands of my job clawed at my attention, refusing to let go.
